Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, who brought the Quran down, or to Allah's angels and messengers, has Allah as his enemy; only the defiantly disobedient deny His clear verses.
Those who conceal what Allah sent down of the Book for a small price fill their bellies with Fire, having exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment.
They turn from every sign and mock the truth, though generations before were destroyed for their sins; even a written scripture would be called magic, and they demand an angel.
Some listen with covered hearts and deaf ears, would not believe any sign, call the revelation legends of former peoples, and keep others away from the Prophet, destroying only themselves.
Allah can send the sign they demand; every creature and bird forms a community gathered to its Lord, while deniers of His verses are deaf and dumb in darkness.
The Prophet's people deny the truth; he is to turn from those who talk offensively of the verses, leave those who take religion as amusement, and remind with the Quran.
They swear they would believe if a sign came, but they would not, even if angels came down and the dead spoke to them, unless Allah willed.
One given Allah's signs detached from them, was pursued by Satan and followed his desire, like a dog panting whether chased or left: the example of deniers of the signs.
Deniers of the signs are led on gradually and given time; their companion is no madman but a warner, and whom Allah sends astray has no guide.
They boast they could say the like of the verses, call them legends and ask for stones from the sky; Allah would not punish them with the Prophet among them.
Every messenger to the former peoples was ridiculed; denial enters the criminals' hearts, and even a gate opened into heaven would be called dazzled eyes and magic.
Though the Quran gives every kind of example, man is most argumentative, and disbelievers mock the verses; their hearts are covered, but their punishment is deferred to an appointed time.
One who disbelieved in Allah's verses claims he will be given wealth and children, but his words are recorded, his punishment extended, and he will come to Allah alone.
Whoever turns from Allah's remembrance has a depressed life and is raised blind, forgotten as he forgot Allah's signs, and the Hereafter's punishment is more severe.
As their reckoning nears, people hear revelation heedlessly, call the Prophet a mere human and it magic, dreams, invention or poetry, and demand a sign, though destroyed cities never believed.
When Allah's clear verses are recited, disbelievers show disapproval and almost attack the reciters, and they are told the Fire promised to disbelievers is worse.
These are verses of the clear Book; the Prophet grieves at their disbelief, but they turn from every new revelation and will learn the news of what they ridiculed.
The criminals will not believe in it until the painful punishment comes suddenly; years of enjoyment will not help them, and no city was destroyed without warners.
Given the truth, they demand what Moses was given and call both scriptures magic; challenged to bring better guidance, they follow desires, though the Quran was conveyed to remind them.
The Quran gives every kind of example, yet whatever sign is brought, disbelievers call believers falsifiers, and so Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know.
Some buy amusing talk to mislead from Allah's way without knowledge, ridicule it, and turn arrogantly from His verses as if deaf, facing humiliating and painful punishment.
None is more unjust than one reminded of his Lord's verses who turns away, and Allah will take retribution from the criminals.
Those who strive against Allah's verses to make them fail will be brought into the punishment.
When the verses are recited, disbelievers say a man wants to turn them from their fathers' worship, call it an invented lie and obvious magic, though they had no scripture.
Only disbelievers dispute Allah's signs; Noah's people and later factions also denied, plotted against their messengers and were seized, and the disbelievers are companions of the Fire.
Those who dispute Allah's signs and deny the Book will be dragged in chains through boiling water into the Fire, find their partners gone, and enter Hell's gates forever.
Companions make their sins attractive; disbelievers urge others to speak noisily over the Quran, and in the Fire they ask to trample the jinn and men who misled them.
Woe to every sinful liar who hears Allah's verses yet persists arrogantly or takes them in ridicule; Hell is before him, while this Quran is guidance.
The Hour has come near and the moon has split, yet seeing a miracle they turn away calling it passing magic, follow their inclinations, and warning does not avail them.
Allah will lead those who deny the Quran gradually to punishment and give them time; they are asked whether a payment burdens them or they know the unseen.
A man given wealth and children still wants more, though obstinate toward Allah's verses; after deliberating he frowned, turned away in arrogance and called it imitated magic and human speech.
